notes: Brokk reads these rules before dispatching an Eindri and passes only concrete --harness/--model/--effort flags to bin/einherjar-spawn.sh. opencode is the primary Ymir harness; pi is the verified secondary harness. Model tokens must match a model opencode/pi can run on this host, or be omitted to use the harness default. effort values: low|medium|high|xhigh|max.

rules.when: General implementation, refactoring, or bug fixes in a codebase
rules.why: opencode is the primary Ymir harness; the flash model is the verified build model for implementation work

rules.when: Deep investigation, diagnosis, planning, or ambiguous design work requiring deep reasoning
rules.why: Maximum reasoning for open-ended investigation and design work on the primary harness

rules.when: Trivial mechanical edits such as rote renames, formatting sweeps, or simple file gathering
rules.why: Fast, cheap profile for narrow low-ambiguity tasks

rules.when: Long-running autonomous or background execution: supervision branches, unattended sweeps, or persistent workers
rules.why: Pi is the verified secondary Ymir harness for persistent and background workers; omitting model uses Pi's configured default

rules.when: The Allfather names a model, a family/quant, or a locality (local/online)
rules.why: Resolve a friendly request to an exact servable id: local -> pi, online -> opencode. If it returns unresolved (or the requested quant is unavailable, e.g. 'iq2' -> nearest), ASK the Allfather with ask_user_question; never guess. Local runs are serialized by bin/local-model-lock.sh.
